contents.html: The NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-90 series supports the generation of high-quality random bits for cryptographic and non-cryptographic use. The security strength of a random number generator depends on the unpredictability of its outputs. This unpredictability can be measured in terms of entropy, which the NIST SP 800-90 series measures using min-entropy. A full-entropy bitstring has an amount of entropy equal to its length. Full-entropy bitstrings are important for cryptographic applications, as these bitstrings have ideal randomness properties and may be used for any cryptographic purpose. Due to the difficulty of generating and testing full-entropy bitstrings, the SP 800-90 series assumes that a bitstring has full entropy if the amount of entropy per bit is at least \(1 - \varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\) is at most \(2^{-32}\). This report provides a justification for the selection of this value of \(\varepsilon\).
contents.html_ja: NIST Special Publication（SP）800-90 シリーズは、暗号用途および非暗号用途に使う高品質な乱数ビットの生成を支援します。乱数生成器のセキュリティ強度は、その出力の予測不可能性に依存します。この予測不可能性はエントロピーで測ることができ、NIST SP 800-90 シリーズでは最小エントロピーを用いて予測不可能性を測定します。完全エントロピーのビット列とは、エントロピーの量がその長さに等しいビット列です。完全エントロピーのビット列は理想的な乱数性を備え、あらゆる暗号用途に使用できるため、暗号アプリケーションにとって重要です。ただし、完全エントロピーのビット列は生成も検査も困難であることから、SP 800-90 シリーズでは、1ビットあたりのエントロピーの量が少なくとも \(1 - \varepsilon\)（\(\varepsilon\) は高々 \(2^{-32}\)）であれば、そのビット列は完全エントロピーを持つと仮定します。本報告書は、この \(\varepsilon\) の値を選定した根拠を示します。

contents.html: The NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-90 series [1][2][3] supports the generation of high-quality random bits for cryptographic and non-cryptographic use. The security strength of a random number generator depends on the unpredictability of its outputs. This unpredictability can be measured in terms of entropy, which the NIST SP 800-90 series measures using min-entropy. The SP 800-90 series refers to certain bitstrings as having full entropy, meaning that they have an amount of entropy equal to their length. Such bitstrings are important for cryptographic applications since they have the highest level of unpredictability and may therefore be used for any cryptographic purpose. The SP 800-90 series assumes that a bitstring has full entropy if the amount of entropy per bit is at least \(1 - \varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\) is at most \(2^{-32}\). This report provides a justification for the selection of this value of \(\varepsilon\). Due to the difficulty of ensuring full entropy through the analysis of random bit generators and sample data sequences, this is accomplished by using an alternative definition of full entropy and calculating the resulting entropy level when this definition is satisfied.
contents.html_ja: NIST Special Publication（SP）800-90 シリーズ [1][2][3] は、暗号用途および非暗号用途に使う高品質な乱数ビットの生成を支援します。乱数生成器のセキュリティ強度は、その出力の予測不可能性に依存します。この予測不可能性はエントロピーで測ることができ、NIST SP 800-90 シリーズでは最小エントロピーを用いて測定します。SP 800-90 シリーズでは、エントロピーの量がその長さに等しいビット列を、完全エントロピーを持つビット列と呼びます。このようなビット列は予測不可能性が最も高く、あらゆる暗号用途に使用できるため、暗号アプリケーションにとって重要です。SP 800-90 シリーズでは、1ビットあたりのエントロピーの量が少なくとも \(1 - \varepsilon\)（\(\varepsilon\) は高々 \(2^{-32}\)）であれば、そのビット列は完全エントロピーを持つと仮定します。本報告書は、この \(\varepsilon\) の値を選定した根拠を示します。乱数ビット生成器やサンプルデータ列の解析によって完全エントロピーを確保することは困難であるため、完全エントロピーの代替的な定義を用い、この定義が満たされるときに得られるエントロピーの水準を計算することで、この根拠を示します。

contents.html: The SP 800-90 series uses a definition of full entropy that prescribes a numerical threshold on the entropy per bit (at least \(1 - \varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\) is at most \(2^{-32}\)). However, although this is an intuitive way to define full entropy, it is generally not possible to ensure sufficient entropy within this tolerance by analyzing a Random Bit Generator (RBG) or estimating entropy from a data sample. It is, therefore, necessary to use a different definition from which a practical approach to ensuring full entropy can be derived. The report begins by defining full entropy in terms of a hypothetical distinguishing game. The report then presents and proves two results following from this definition. First, it is shown how output satisfying this definition can be generated using a vetted conditioning function (see [2]) acting on data having an entropy level that meets or exceeds a certain value. Second, it is shown that the entropy level of output produced by such a process satisfies the full entropy threshold used in the SP 800-90 series, thereby demonstrating a connection between these two definitions.
contents.html_ja: SP 800-90 シリーズは、1ビットあたりのエントロピーに数値のしきい値（少なくとも \(1 - \varepsilon\)、ここで \(\varepsilon\) は高々 \(2^{-32}\)）を定める完全エントロピーの定義を用いています。しかし、これは完全エントロピーを定義する直感的な方法ではあるものの、乱数ビット生成器（RBG）を解析したり、データサンプルからエントロピーを推定したりして、この許容範囲内で十分なエントロピーを確保することは、一般に不可能です。そのため、完全エントロピーを確保する実用的な方法を導ける別の定義を用いる必要があります。本報告書はまず、仮想的な識別ゲームによって完全エントロピーを定義します。次に、この定義から導かれる二つの結果を示して証明します。第一に、この定義を満たす出力を、一定値以上のエントロピー水準を持つデータに対して審査済みコンディショニング関数（[2] を参照）を適用することで生成できることを示します。第二に、このような処理で生成した出力のエントロピー水準が、SP 800-90 シリーズで用いる完全エントロピーのしきい値を満たすことを示し、二つの定義の間の関係を明らかにします。

contents.html: Full entropy will be defined as follows. Consider a distinguishing game where an adversary attempts to distinguish between two cases – REAL and IDEAL. Assume that the adversary is provided with \(W\) \(n\)-bit outputs \(b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_W\). In the REAL case, each output is generated by a cryptographic conditioning function operating on an output from a real-life entropy source. In the IDEAL case, the outputs are generated by an idealized randomness source that produces independent \(n\)-bit outputs with each output value having a probability of \(2^{-n}\). One of the two cases is chosen at random with each being equally likely. Outputs of length \(n\) bits generated in the REAL case are defined as having full entropy with respect to \(W\) and \(\delta\) (where \(\delta > 0\)) if a computationally unlimited adversary cannot correctly distinguish between the REAL and IDEAL cases with probability higher than \(\frac{1}{2} + \delta\).
contents.html_ja: 完全エントロピーを次のように定義します。攻撃者が二つの場合、すなわち REAL と IDEAL を識別しようとする識別ゲームを考えます。攻撃者に、\(n\) ビットの出力 \(W\) 個 \(b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_W\) が与えられるものとします。REAL の場合、各出力は、現実のエントロピー源の出力に暗号学的コンディショニング関数を適用して生成されます。IDEAL の場合、各出力は、各出力値の確率が \(2^{-n}\) である独立な \(n\) ビットの出力を生成する理想化された乱数源によって生成されます。二つの場合のうち一方が、等しい確率でランダムに選ばれます。REAL の場合に生成された長さ \(n\) ビットの出力は、計算能力に制限のない攻撃者が REAL と IDEAL を \(\frac{1}{2} + \delta\) より高い確率で正しく識別できないとき、\(W\) と \(\delta\)（\(\delta > 0\)）に関して完全エントロピーを持つと定義します。

contents.html: It is assumed in SP 800-90C that there is an upper bound of \(2^{64}\) bits on the amount of output that an adversary attempting a distinguishing attack can obtain. Consider the combination \(W = 2^{48}\) and \(\delta = 2^{-10}\). Given \(W = 2^{48}\) \(n\)-bit RBG outputs, each output can be up to \(2^{16} = 65536\) bits long without exceeding the \(2^{64}\) data-quantity bound. Note that 10000 RBGs –each producing 1000 outputs per second– would require nearly a year to produce \(W = 2^{48}\) outputs. According to the table above, an adversary who obtains \(W = 2^{48}\) \(n\)-bit outputs has a distinguishing probability no greater than \(\frac{1}{2} + \delta = \frac{1}{2} + 2^{-10} \cong 0.501\) when \(H\), the conditioning function input min-entropy for each \(n\)-bit output, is at least \(n + 63.3\). This minimum value, rounded up to \(n + 64\), is used in this document and in SP 800-90C as the condition for satisfying the full entropy definition.

contents.html: The proof of Claim 1 uses a test statistic \(X\) computed from data values generated in either the REAL or the IDEAL case. It will be assumed that \(X\) is approximately normally distributed. This statistic is of the form \(X = \sum_{i=1}^{W} x_i\), where the variables \(x_i\) are independent and identically distributed, and depend on the observed values \(b_i\). If \(\mu_x\) and \(\sigma_x^2\) are the true mean and variance of the individual variables \(x_i\), respectively (\(\mu_x\) and \(\sigma_x^2\) are derived in A.1), then \(\frac{\frac{X}{W} - \mu_x}{\left(\sigma_x / \sqrt{W}\right)} = \frac{\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{W} x_i}{W} - \mu_x}{\left(\sigma_x / \sqrt{W}\right)}\) is approximately normally distributed by the Central Limit Theorem when \(W\) is large (we assume \(W = 2^{48}\)). Since \(X\) can be obtained from \(\frac{\frac{X}{W} - \mu_x}{\left(\sigma_x / \sqrt{W}\right)}\) by a linear transformation, \(X\) is also approximately normally distributed.

contents.html: The discussion of full entropy in this paper is in the context of the SP 800-90 series, where bit sequences having full entropy are to be generated by processing entropy source output sequences (that generally do not have full entropy) with a vetted conditioning function or a Deterministic Random Bit Generator (DRBG). The assumption below is made in that context.
contents.html_ja: 本論文における完全エントロピーの議論は SP 800-90 シリーズの文脈におけるものであり、そこでは、完全エントロピーを持つビット列は、（一般には完全エントロピーを持たない）エントロピー源の出力列を、審査済みコンディショニング関数または決定論的乱数ビット生成器（DRBG）で処理して生成されます。以下の仮定は、この文脈で置くものです。

contents.html: Suppose that a conditioning function generates an \(n\)-bit output by processing a sequence from an entropy source. Consider the probability \(p_j\) for the \(j^{th}\) possible output value from the conditioning function. These probabilities are determined by the interaction between the specific conditioning function used and the space of possible inputs to that function. In the distinguishing game used in the full entropy definition, the adversary has complete knowledge of the conditioning function and its input space, and—being computationally unlimited—can determine the probabilities \(p_j\). For the purposes of this paper, determining the values of these probabilities is infeasible. However, it is useful to consider the \(p_j\) as random variables rather than fixed values and use statistics associated with these random variables to find the probability distribution of the test statistic \(X\). This can be justified as follows. Consider the application of the conditioning function to the input space of entropy source sequences to obtain the conditioning function output. The resulting mapping depends on both the selected input domain and the details of the conditioning function. The domain of this function is determined by the characteristics of the entropy source and the length of the entropy source sequences that are input to the conditioning function. These details effectively select from a large number of possible domains for the function. A consequence of the cryptographic properties of conditioning functions used in RBGs is that there is no simple pattern in the mapping from elements of the domain to elements of the range of the function, and there is no discernible bias in the assignment of outputs to inputs. Therefore, although the conditioning function is deterministic, this report will assume that it is effectively a mapping that assigns an \(n\)-bit output to each value in the domain with a uniform distribution so that each possible output value has a probability of \(2^{-n}\) of being the output value assigned to a given input value. (Note that multiple input values can be assigned a given output value.) Under this assumption, since probability \(p_j\) is the sum of the probabilities of the inputs mapped to the \(j^{th}\) output value, the probability \(p_j\) can be treated as a random variable.
contents.html_ja: コンディショニング関数が、エントロピー源からの列を処理して \(n\) ビットの出力を生成するとします。コンディショニング関数の \(j\) 番目の出力値の確率 \(p_j\) を考えます。これらの確率は、使用する具体的なコンディショニング関数と、その関数への入力として可能な空間との相互作用によって決まります。完全エントロピーの定義で用いる識別ゲームでは、攻撃者はコンディショニング関数とその入力空間を完全に知っており、計算能力に制限がないため、確率 \(p_j\) を求めることができます。本論文の目的上、これらの確率の値を求めることは実行不可能です。しかし、\(p_j\) を固定値ではなく確率変数とみなし、これらの確率変数に関する統計量を用いて検定統計量 \(X\) の確率分布を求めることは有用です。これは次のように正当化できます。エントロピー源の列からなる入力空間にコンディショニング関数を適用して、コンディショニング関数の出力を得ることを考えます。得られる写像は、選択した入力の定義域と、コンディショニング関数の詳細の両方に依存します。この関数の定義域は、エントロピー源の特性と、コンディショニング関数に入力されるエントロピー源の列の長さによって決まります。これらの詳細は、この関数の非常に多くの可能な定義域の中から一つを事実上選択します。RBG で使用されるコンディショニング関数の暗号学的性質の帰結として、定義域の要素から関数の値域の要素への写像には単純なパターンがなく、入力への出力の割り当てに識別できる偏りもありません。したがって、コンディショニング関数は決定論的ではあるものの、本報告書では、これは定義域の各値に対して一様分布で \(n\) ビットの出力を割り当てる写像と事実上みなせるものとし、各出力値が、与えられた入力値に割り当てられる出力値となる確率は \(2^{-n}\) であるとします（複数の入力値に同じ出力値が割り当てられる場合があることに注意してください）。この仮定の下では、確率 \(p_j\) は \(j\) 番目の出力値に写像される入力の確率の総和であるため、\(p_j\) は確率変数として扱えます。

contents.html: Consider that \(p_j\) is treated as a random variable as explained in Assumption 2. Suppose that there are \(M\) possible inputs to the conditioning function, with probabilities \(\{q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_M\}\). (Note that no assumptions will be made on the input probability distribution.) The output probability \(p_j\) can then be written as \(p_j = \sum_{i=1}^{M} q_i I_{i,j}\), where \(I_{i,j} = 1\) if the conditioning function maps the \(i^{\text{th}}\) input to the \(j^{\text{th}}\) output, and \(I_{i,j} = 0\) otherwise. Under Assumption 2, the assignment of inputs to outputs is done independently for each input, so for each value of \(j\), the variables \(q_i I_{i,j}\) are independent. The value of \(M\) is dependent on the characteristics of the entropy source outputs and the bit length of the conditioning function input. However, it is reasonable to assume that \(M\) is at least \(2^n\), the number of possible conditioning function outputs (it would be difficult to achieve a level of output entropy near \(n\) otherwise). Given the above statements, \(p_j\) is of a similar form to that of \(X\) in Assumption 1 and, according to a version of the Central Limit Theorem applying to independent random variables not having the same distribution, can be assumed to be approximately normally distributed.
contents.html_ja: 仮定2で説明したとおり、\(p_j\) を確率変数として扱うことを考えます。コンディショニング関数への可能な入力が \(M\) 個あり、その確率が \(\{q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_M\}\) であるとします（入力の確率分布には何の仮定も置かないことに注意してください）。このとき、出力確率 \(p_j\) は \(p_j = \sum_{i=1}^{M} q_i I_{i,j}\) と書けます。ここで、\(I_{i,j} = 1\) はコンディショニング関数が \(i\) 番目の入力を \(j\) 番目の出力に写像する場合、\(I_{i,j} = 0\) はそれ以外の場合です。仮定2の下では、入力への出力の割り当ては入力ごとに独立に行われるため、各 \(j\) の値について、変数 \(q_i I_{i,j}\) は独立です。\(M\) の値は、エントロピー源の出力の特性と、コンディショニング関数の入力のビット長に依存します。しかし、\(M\) は少なくとも、コンディショニング関数の可能な出力の数である \(2^n\) であると仮定するのが妥当です（そうでなければ、出力エントロピーを \(n\) に近い水準にすることは困難です）。以上から、\(p_j\) は仮定1の \(X\) と同様の形をしており、同一分布に従わない独立な確率変数に適用される中心極限定理の一形式により、おおよそ正規分布に従うと仮定できます。

contents.html: A.2. Justification of the Claim on Higher Powers of \(\theta_j\)

contents.html: In the proof of Claim 1, sums of the powers of \(\theta_j\) higher than \(\theta_j^2\) were omitted. This does not affect the validity of the conclusion if \(\theta_j\) is sufficiently near zero. This is established as follows. Recall that there are \(2^n\) values of \(\theta_j\), each of which is approximately normally distributed with mean zero and variance approximately \(2^{n-H_2}\). Consider the largest \(\theta_j\): \(\theta_{max} = \max_j\{\theta_j\}\). \(\theta_{max}\) is \(z = \frac{\theta_{max}}{2^{\frac{n-H_2}{2}}}\) standard deviations away from zero (which was shown in A.1 to be the mean of \(\theta_j\)). The value of \(z\) is expected to be such that in a collection of \(2^n\) standard normal random variates, approximately one of the variates is greater than or equal to this value of \(z\). If \(f(z)\) and \(F(z)\) are the density function and the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution, respectively, then for large \(z\), \(1 - F(z) \cong \frac{f(z)}{z}\) (see Section 26.2.12 of [4]). The desired value of \(z\), therefore, gives \((1 - F(z))2^n \cong 1\), which leads to \(\frac{2^n}{z\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{z^2}{2}} = 1\), or \(z^2 + 2\ln z = 2n\ln 2 - \ln(2\pi)\). Since \(z^2\) dominates the left side of this equation for moderately large values of \(z\), the desired value of \(z\) is approximately \(\sqrt{2n\ln 2 - \ln(2\pi)}\). The value of \(\theta_{max}\) is then expected to be approximately \(2^{\frac{n-H_2}{2}}\sqrt{2n\ln 2 - \ln(2\pi)}\). For any of the typical values of \(n\) and a value of \(H_2\) given by the lower bound established in Claim 1, \(H_2 \ge n + 64\), so \(2^{\frac{n-H_2}{2}} \le 2^{-32}\), and it can be calculated that \(\theta_{max}\) is a positive value that is likely to be less than \(10^{-8}\). A similar argument leads to \(\theta_{min}\) being approximately \(-\theta_{max}\), so it is expected that \(|\theta_j| \le 10^{-8}\) for all \(j\). Therefore, it is safe to omit powers of \(\theta_j\) higher than \(\theta_j^2\), since it is shown in A.1 that doing so has a negligible effect.
contents.html_ja: 主張1の証明では、\(\theta_j^2\) より高次の \(\theta_j\) の冪の和を省略しました。\(\theta_j\) が十分にゼロに近ければ、これは結論の妥当性に影響しません。これは次のように示せます。\(\theta_j\) の値が \(2^n\) 個あり、それぞれがおおよそ平均ゼロ、分散がおおよそ \(2^{n-H_2}\) の正規分布に従うことを思い出してください。最大の \(\theta_j\)、すなわち \(\theta_{max} = \max_j\{\theta_j\}\) を考えます。\(\theta_{max}\) は、ゼロ（A.1 で \(\theta_j\) の平均であることが示されました）から \(z = \frac{\theta_{max}}{2^{\frac{n-H_2}{2}}}\) 標準偏差分だけ離れています。\(z\) の値は、\(2^n\) 個の標準正規確率変量の集まりの中で、おおよそ1個の変量がこの \(z\) の値以上になるような値であると期待されます。\(f(z)\) と \(F(z)\) をそれぞれ標準正規分布の密度関数と累積分布関数とすると、\(z\) が大きいとき \(1 - F(z) \cong \frac{f(z)}{z}\) です（[4] の Section 26.2.12 を参照）。したがって、求める \(z\) の値は \((1 - F(z))2^n \cong 1\) を満たし、これより \(\frac{2^n}{z\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{z^2}{2}} = 1\)、すなわち \(z^2 + 2\ln z = 2n\ln 2 - \ln(2\pi)\) が得られます。\(z\) がある程度大きい値であれば、この式の左辺では \(z^2\) が支配的であるため、求める \(z\) の値はおおよそ \(\sqrt{2n\ln 2 - \ln(2\pi)}\) です。すると、\(\theta_{max}\) はおおよそ \(2^{\frac{n-H_2}{2}}\sqrt{2n\ln 2 - \ln(2\pi)}\) であると期待されます。典型的な \(n\) の値と、主張1で確立した下界 \(H_2 \ge n + 64\) を満たす \(H_2\) の値については、\(2^{\frac{n-H_2}{2}} \le 2^{-32}\) であり、\(\theta_{max}\) は \(10^{-8}\) 未満である可能性が高い正の値であると計算できます。同様の議論により、\(\theta_{min}\) はおおよそ \(-\theta_{max}\) となるため、すべての \(j\) について \(|\theta_j| \le 10^{-8}\) であると期待されます。したがって、\(\theta_j^2\) より高次の \(\theta_j\) の冪を省略しても、A.1 で示したとおり影響は無視できるほど小さいため、安全に省略できます。

contents.html:
ideal randomness source
The source of an ideal random sequence of bits. Each bit of an ideal random sequence is unpredictable and unbiased, with a value that is independent of the values of the other bits in the sequence. Prior to an observation of the sequence, the value of each bit is equally likely to be 0 or 1, and the probability that a particular bit will have a particular value is unaffected by knowledge of the values of any or all of the other bits. An ideal random sequence of \(n\) bits contains \(n\) bits of entropy.

ideal randomness source
理想的な乱数ビット列の源。理想的な乱数ビット列の各ビットは予測不可能かつ偏りがなく、その値は列中の他のビットの値から独立しています。列を観測する前の各ビットの値は、0である確率と1である確率が等しく、特定のビットが特定の値を取る確率は、他のビットの一部または全部の値を知っても変わりません。\(n\) ビットの理想的な乱数列は、\(n\) ビットのエントロピーを含みます。

A lower bound on the entropy of a random variable. The precise formulation for min-entropy is \((-\log_2 \max p_i)\) for a discrete distribution having probabilities \(p_1, \ldots, p_k\). Min-entropy is often used as a measure of the unpredictability of a random variable.

The NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-90 series supports the generation of high-quality random bits for cryptographic and non-cryptographic use. The security strength of a random number generator depends on the unpredictability of its outputs. This unpredictability can be measured in terms of entropy, which the NIST SP 800-90 series measures using min-entropy. A full-entropy bitstring has an amount of entropy equal to its length. Full-entropy bitstrings are important for cryptographic applications, as these bitstrings have ideal randomness properties and may be used for any cryptographic purpose. Due to the difficulty of generating and testing full-entropy bitstrings, the SP 800-90 series assumes that a bitstring has full entropy if the amount of entropy per bit is at least 1 − ε, where ε is at most 2−32. This report provides a justification for the selection of this value of ε.

The NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-90 series [1][2][3] supports the generation of high-quality random bits for cryptographic and non-cryptographic use. The security strength of a random number generator depends on the unpredictability of its outputs. This unpredictability can be measured in terms of entropy, which the NIST SP 800-90 series measures using min-entropy. The SP 800-90 series refers to certain bitstrings as having full entropy, meaning that they have an amount of entropy equal to their length. Such bitstrings are important for cryptographic applications since they have the highest level of unpredictability and may therefore be used for any cryptographic purpose. The SP 800-90 series assumes that a bitstring has full entropy if the amount of entropy per bit is at least 1 −ε, where ε is at most 2−32. This report provides a justification for the selection of this value ofε. Due to the difficulty of ensuring full entropy through the analysis of random bit generators and sample data sequences, this is accomplished by using an alternative definition of full entropy and calculating the resulting entropy level when this definition is satisfied.

The SP 800-90 series uses a definition of full entropy that prescribes a numerical threshold on the entropy per bit (at least 1 − ε, where ε is at most 2−32). However, although this is an intuitive way to define full entropy, it is generally not possible to ensure sufficient entropy within this tolerance by analyzing a Random Bit Generator (RBG) or estimating entropy from a data sample. It is, therefore, necessary to use a different definition from which a practical approach to ensuring full entropy can be derived. The report begins by defining full entropy in terms of a hypothetical distinguishing game. The report then presents and proves two results following from this definition. First, it is shown how output satisfying this definition can be generated using a vetted conditioning function (see [2]) acting on data having an entropy level that meets or exceeds a certain value. Second, it is shown that the entropy level of output produced by such a process satisfies the full entropy threshold used in the SP 800-90 series, thereby demonstrating a connection between these two definitions.

Appendix B. List of Symbols, Abbreviations, and Acronyms
NIST National Institute of Standards and Technology
ε A positive constant that is assumed to be no greater than 2−32
E(X) The expected value of the random variable X
Var(x) Variance of random variable x
adversary A malicious entity whose goal is to determine, to guess, or to influence the output of an RBG.
bitstring An ordered sequence (string) of 0s and 1s. The leftmost bit is the most significant bit.
conditioning function A deterministic function used to reduce bias and/or improve the entropy per bit.

cryptographic boundary An explicitly defined physical or conceptual perimeter that establishes the physical and/or logical bounds of a cryptographic module and contains all of the hardware, software, and/or firmware components of a cryptographic module.
entropy A measure of the randomness or uncertainty of a random variable.
entropy source The combination of a noise source, health tests, and optional conditioning component that produce bitstrings containing entropy.

full-entropy bitstring A bitstring with ideal randomness (i.e., the amount of entropy per bit is equal to 1). This publication proves that a bitstring satisfying a certain definition of full entropy has an entropy rate of at least 1 − ε, where ε is at most 2−32.

ideal randomness source The source of an ideal random sequence of bits. Each bit of an ideal random sequence is unpredictable and unbiased, with a value that is independent of the values of the other bits in the sequence. Prior to an observation of the sequence, the value of each bit is equally likely to be 0 or 1, and the probability that a particular bit will have a particular value is unaffected by knowledge of the values of any or all of the other bits. An ideal random sequence of n bits contains n bits of entropy.

likelihood ratio test A statistical test aimed at distinguishing between two competing models that could have produced an observed event based on a comparison of the likelihoods of the observed event, given the two models.

min-entropy A lower bound on the entropy of a random variable. The precise formulation for min-entropy is (−log max p ) for a discrete distribution having probabilities p , ..., p . Min-entropy is often used
as a measure of the unpredictability of a random variable.
